_comment: mouse.json plus a third step that subdivides NREM into NREM2, NREM3 and TR (transition). Same idea as the human recipe: once a stage is isolated, refit a PCA inside just those epochs so the components describe what is left to resolve rather than the wake/sleep difference that has already been settled. Collapsing back to three stages recovers plain WAKE/NREM/REM, so a substage run can still be compared against an ordinary rodent reference: nyx.collapse(result.hypnogram, 3).

steps._comment: As mouse.json: NREM and REM out of sleep.
steps.name: split_sleep

steps._comment: Subdivide NREM. gmm with a fixed n_clusters rather than hdbscan: the three substages are not separated by a density gap the way NREM and REM are, so letting the algorithm decide how many there are gives a different count on every recording. stage_order runs from lowest to highest centroid on the first PC; this one is taken from the run it was developed on, and the sign of a principal component is arbitrary, so it is NOT a safe default. CHECK THE PER-CLUSTER PSDs and reorder if they disagree -- substage boundaries are far less clear-cut than NREM/REM, and this is the step most worth overriding.
steps.name: split_nrem
